text:
maria: Heads-up: the docs for POST /v1/files/upload list 'metadata' as an object ( { "project": "alpha" } ) but our S3 connector expects an array of key/value objects. Support just got a 400 on a customer ticket. :grimacing:
aj: Do we have the exact failing curl?
maria: Yep. From support:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/files/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"file_url":"https://...","metadata":{"owner":"alice","env":"prod"}}'
```
Response: 400 {"error":"invalid metadata format"}
kevin: I checked the runtime: we accept an array like `[{"key":"owner","value":"alice"}]`. OpenAPI currently uses `additionalProperties: true` which models an object — that's the mismatch. I'll open a PR to change the schema to `array` with items `{ key, value }` and add examples.
docs-bot: kevin opened PR #2345: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2345
samir: Before we merge we need to check SDKs. Python's client will happily serialize a dict; Go's json marshaler too. Add migration notes and snippet to docs so devs can adapt.
aj: Can the server be lenient and accept both forms for now?
maria: Ops confirmed they can accept object forms for requests sent to api versions <= v1.2, but will remove the fallback in ~90 days. Docs must be explicit about deprecation and show how to transform payloads.
kevin: Drafted PR includes:
```
# python transform
if isinstance(metadata, dict):
    metadata = [{"key": k, "value": v} for k, v in metadata.items()]
```
and a Go snippet using a small helper convertMetadata(map[string]string) -> []Metadata. Added examples for curl, python, and js.
aj: LGTM. Add a small note about duplicate keys: object loses duplicates/ordering, array preserves them.
samir: Also add a docs CI test that validates the example payloads against the OpenAPI schema so this doesn't regress.
maria: I'll coordinate a short support announcement and the changelog blurb. Thanks everyone :tada:
docs-bot: Merged in staging, will schedule prod deploy after CI passes.
